about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Pilau Spiced Beef and Potato Rice Pot
recipes.summary: A fragrant one-pot rice, browned beef and potatoes cooked in whole spices and a deep onion base.
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the thinly sliced onions with 1 tsp salt for 15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown.
Add the beef and brown for 8 minutes until coloured all over. Stir in the crushed garlic, grated ginger, cumin, pepper and cinnamon and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 3 cups water, cover and simmer on low for 40 minutes until the beef is tender.

Add the potato chunks and rinsed rice with 2 1/2 cups water. Bring to the boil, stir once, cover and cook on very low heat for 18 minutes until the rice is tender and fluffy and the water is absorbed.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff and serve. The beef should reach at least 75°C.
notes: Food safety: cook beef pieces to 75°C and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: do not skip the slow browning of the onions, as they give the colour and sweetness.

recipes.title: Swahili Fish in Coconut Tamarind Sauce
recipes.summary: White fish simmered in a tangy coconut and tamarind sauce, served over rice.
steps: Cook the rice in 1 1/2 cups water, covered, on low heat for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the sliced onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add garlic and turmeric for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomato and cook for 5 minutes until broken down, then pour in the coconut milk, tamarind and 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Lay the fish in the sauce and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until opaque and flaking at 63°C.
Serve the fish and sauce over the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook fish to 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Nairobi Style Beef Curry with Coconut Finish
recipes.summary: Tender beef simmered with spices and coconut until the sauce clings to the meat, served with rice.
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onions for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant, then the beef and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the chopped tomato, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 cup water, cover and simmer for 35 minutes until the beef is tender, reaching at least 75°C.
Uncover, stir in the coconut milk and cook for 5 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings to the beef.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve alongside.
notes: Food safety: cook beef to 75°C; refrigerate leftovers promptly.

recipes.title: Ugali with Spiced Egg and Tomato Stew
recipes.summary: Firm maize porridge with a simple tomato stew cooked with whole eggs.
steps: Boil the water with 1/2 tsp salt and whisk in the polenta. Cook on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring hard, until very thick and pulling away from the pot.
Meanwhile fry the sliced onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the curry powder and chopped tomato and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Make three wells in the stew, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 minutes until the whites are set.
Shape the ugali into mounds and serve with the stew.
notes: Food safety: cook eggs until set.

recipes.title: Mchuzi Mix Coconut Chicken Wraps
recipes.summary: Chicken simmered in a mild coconut curry sauce and wrapped in warm chapati with kachumbari.
steps: Fry the onion in a little oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the curry powder for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken, tomato and 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is cooked through at 75°C.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Finely dice the cucumber and red onion with a pinch of salt for a quick kachumbari.
Warm the chapati until soft and fill with chicken and kachumbari.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Zanzibar Spiced Potato and Pea Patties
recipes.summary: Crisp potato cakes with peas and cumin, shallow-fried and served with a lime wedge.
steps: Boil the potato for 15 minutes until tender, drain and mash roughly. Cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the mash with the peas, cumin, turmeric, egg, flour and 1 tsp salt until it holds together when pressed into a ball. Chill for 10 minutes so the patties firm up.
Shape into 8 patties and fry in the oil for 4 minutes a side over medium heat until golden brown and crisp.
Serve warm with lime wedges.
notes: Food safety: cook until set in the middle.

recipes.title: Cape Malay Style Chicken Biryani Pot
recipes.summary: Layered rice and spiced chicken with caramelised onions, cooked slowly so the grains stay separate.
steps: Fry the sliced onions in the oil for 15 minutes until deeply golden, then lift half out for the topping.
Add garlic, curry powder, turmeric and cinnamon for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chicken and yoghurt and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken reaches at least 75°C and the sauce is thick.
Boil the rice and lentils in salted water for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Layer half the rice over the chicken, add the rest of the chicken mix, then the remaining rice. Scatter over the fried onion.
Cover tightly and cook on very low heat for 25 minutes until the rice is tender and steamed through.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C and cool leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Durban Style Lamb Curry with Roti
recipes.summary: Slow-cooked lamb curry with potato and a warming spice base, scooped up with roti.
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onions for 8 minutes until golden. Add garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the lamb and brown for 8 minutes, then add tomato, 1 tsp salt and 1 cup water.
Cover and simmer on low for 70 minutes until the lamb is very tender.
Add the potato chunks and cook for 20 minutes until tender, reaching at least 75°C in the lamb.
Warm the roti in a dry pan and serve with the curry.
notes: Food safety: cook lamb to 75°C and reheat leftovers until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Potjie Style Chicken and Butternut Stew
recipes.summary: A gentle one-pot chicken stew with butternut, tomatoes and a hint of apricot.
steps: Brown the chicken in oil for 8 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Fry the onions for 5 minutes until soft, stir in the curry powder, then add tomato and jam and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the chicken with the pumpkin and 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook on low for 35 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C and the pumpkin is tender.
Season with salt and serve with rice or bread.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C.

recipes.title: Curried Chicken Mayo Sandwiches with Apricot Chutney
recipes.summary: Shredded cooked chicken folded through curry mayo and apricot chutney, layered with cucumber in toasted bread.
steps: Toast the bread in a toaster or dry pan for 3 minutes until golden and crisp, then let it cool on a rack so the sandwiches do not turn soggy.
Shred the cooked chicken finely and mix in a bowl with the mayonnaise, curry powder, apricot jam and a pinch of salt until creamy and evenly coated.
Slice the cucumber thinly and pat dry with paper towel.
Spread the chicken mixture over three slices of toast, top with cucumber, then close with the remaining toast and press gently until the filling holds.
Cut into halves or triangles and serve at once, or wrap and chill for up to 4 hours until needed.
notes: Food safety: use chicken that was cooked and chilled promptly; keep refrigerated until eating and discard after 2 days.
Tip: a squeeze of lemon lifts the filling if the jam is very sweet.

recipes.title: Prawn Sambal Plates with Crisp Sweet Corn Cakes
recipes.summary: Crisp sweet corn fritters served over fluffy rice with fiery sambal prawns.
steps: Rinse 1 cup of dry jasmine rice, then cook with 1 1/2 cups water in a covered pot on low heat for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy. Rest covered for 5 minutes.
Stir the corn, flour, egg, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 cup water into a thick, spoonable batter.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Drop in heaped spoonfuls of batter and fry for 3 minutes a side until deep golden and crisp at the edges. Drain on paper towel.
Wipe the pan, heat the remaining oil and stir-fry the prawns with the sambal for 4 minutes until pink, opaque and coated in the glossy sauce.
Divide the rice among bowls, arrange the fritters on top and spoon over the prawns and their sauce.
notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and pink throughout; eat promptly and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: sambal oelek is hot, so use 1 tbsp for a milder bowl.

recipes.title: Malaysian Chicken Curry Puffs with Cucumber
recipes.summary: Flaky pastry half-moons filled with spiced chicken and potato, baked until puffed and deep golden.
steps: Boil the finely diced potato for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain and leave to steam dry.

Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the finely chopped onion for 4 minutes until soft, add the mince and curry powder and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until the mince is cooked through at 75°C and no longer pink.
Stir in the potato and 1/2 tsp salt, then spread on a tray and cool for 15 minutes so the pastry stays crisp.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares, add a spoonful of filling to each, fold into triangles and press the edges with a fork until sealed. Brush with beaten egg.
Bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Serve warm with sliced cucumber.
notes: Food safety: cook mince to 75°C and cool the filling quickly; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: cold filling and cold pastry give the flakiest puffs.

recipes.title: Sambal Tumis Egg and Long Bean Lunch Plates
recipes.summary: Green beans stir-fried in a mild sambal with halved boiled eggs, served over steamed rice.
steps: Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice with 1 1/2 cups water in a covered pot on low heat for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Boil the eggs in simmering water for 8 minutes until the yolks are just set, then cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Heat the oil in a wok or large pan and fry the sliced onion for 4 minutes until soft. Add the sambal and stir for 1 minute until darker and fragrant.
Add the beans cut into 5cm lengths with 1/4 cup water and cook for 6 minutes, tossing, until crisp-tender and coated in sauce.
Divide the rice between plates, top with the beans and the halved eggs, and spoon over any sauce left in the pan.
notes: Food safety: boil eggs until the whites and yolks are firm and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Soto Betawi Style Beef and Coconut Stew
recipes.summary: A rich beef stew in a creamy, spiced coconut broth with potato and tomato.
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the sliced onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the crushed garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beef and ground coriander and stir for 3 minutes to coat. Pour in the water with 1 tsp salt, cover and simmer on low for 70 minutes until the beef is tender when pressed with a fork.
Add the potato chunks and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and wedges of tomato and simmer uncovered for 8 minutes until the broth thickens slightly and the beef reaches at least 75°C.
Taste and add salt, then ladle into bowls with the potato and beef.
notes: Food safety: cook beef to 75°C; reheat leftovers until steaming hot.
Tip: skim the oil that rises to the top for a lighter broth.

recipes.title: Tahu Isi Stuffed Tofu with Peanut Sauce
recipes.summary: Golden fried tofu pockets stuffed with crunchy vegetables and drizzled with creamy peanut sauce.
steps: Press the tofu for 10 minutes, then cut into 8 triangles and pat dry with paper towel.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp on all sides. Drain on paper towel.
Slice a pocket into each piece and stuff with grated carrot and bean sprouts.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice and 1/4 cup warm water until smooth and pourable like cream.
Arrange the tofu on a plate and drizzle with the sauce while the tofu is still warm.
notes: Vegan.
Tip: loosen the sauce with a little more warm water if it thickens.

recipes.title: Pacific Coconut Fish Stew with Sweet Potato
recipes.summary: A gentle fish stew in coconut milk with tender sweet potato and wilted spinach.
steps: Peel and cube the sweet potato and boil for 12 minutes until tender when pierced. Drain and set aside.
Cook the sliced onion with a splash of water in a wide pot for 5 minutes until soft, then add the coconut milk, 1/2 cup water and 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Cut the fish into large chunks, add to the pot and simmer gently for 6 minutes until opaque, flaking easily and at least 63°C.
Stir in the spinach and sweet potato for 1 minute until the spinach wilts, then finish with the lime juice.
Ladle into bowls and serve warm.
notes: Food safety: cook fish to 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Samoan Style Coconut Beef and Potato Hash
recipes.summary: Browned beef mince and crisp potato hash finished with coconut milk and spring onion.
steps: Dice the potatoes small and fry in the oil in a large pan over medium heat for 10 minutes, turning, until golden and tender.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 3 minutes until soft, then add the mince and cook for 6 minutes until browned and cooked through at 75°C.
Pour in the coconut milk with 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 2 minutes until absorbed and creamy.
Scatter with the spring onion and serve straight from the pan.
notes: Food safety: cook mince to 75°C and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Hawaiian Style Seared Fish Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Seared white fish over fluffy rice with sweet pineapple, cucumber and soy.
steps: Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice with 1 1/2 cups water in a covered pot on low heat for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Pat the fish dry and season with salt. Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and sear for 3 minutes a side until golden, opaque and flaking at 63°C.
Slice the cucumber and drain the pineapple.
Break the fish into chunks and arrange over the rice with pineapple and cucumber, then drizzle over the soy sauce.
notes: Food safety: cook fish to 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Gluten Free Tamari Beef and Broccoli
recipes.summary: Tender beef and bright broccoli in a glossy tamari sauce thickened with cornflour, served on rice.
steps: Toss the beef with 1 tsp of the cornflour and 1 tbsp tamari and set aside for 10 minutes.
Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Sear the beef for 2 minutes until browned and 63°C inside, then lift out.
Stir-fry the broccoli florets, crushed garlic and grated ginger for 4 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp.
Mix the remaining tamari and cornflour with 1/2 cup water, pour in and cook for 2 minutes until glossy and thick, then return the beef.
Toss for 30 seconds until hot and serve over the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook beef to 63°C; keep raw meat away from ready-to-eat food.
Check the tamari label is gluten-free.

recipes.title: Gluten Free Rice Noodle Stir-Fry with Tamarind, Prawn and Egg
recipes.summary: Rice noodles with prawns, egg and tamarind in a sweet-sour sauce with peanuts.
steps: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, or to packet directions, until just tender, then drain.
Mix the tamarind, tamari, sugar and 2 tbsp water for the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the prawns for 3 minutes until pink and opaque, push aside and scramble the eggs for 1 minute until set.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 3 minutes until glossy, hot and the noodles have absorbed the sauce.
Toss through the sprouts, then serve topped with crushed peanuts and lime wedges.
notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and eggs until set.
Check the tamari and tamarind labels are gluten-free.

recipes.title: Gluten Free Korean Style Beef Bowls
recipes.summary: Sliced beef marinated in tamari, sesame and garlic, seared and served over rice with cucumber.
steps: Mix the beef with the tamari, sesame oil, sugar and crushed garlic. Set aside for 20 minutes.
Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat and sear the beef in 2 batches for 3 minutes each until browned, caramelised and at least 63°C.
Slice the cucumber and divide with the rice among bowls.
Top with the beef and any pan juices and serve warm.
notes: Plus 20 minutes marinating.
Food safety: cook beef to 63°C and discard leftover marinade.

recipes.title: Gluten Free Japanese Style Ginger Pork with Rice
recipes.summary: Thin pork slices glazed in a ginger, honey and tamari sauce, served with crisp cabbage and rice.
steps: Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the pork in two batches for 3 minutes each until browned and at least 70°C inside.
Add the tamari, honey and grated ginger and bubble for 2 minutes until sticky and glossy.
Finely shred the cabbage and divide with the rice among plates.
Top with the pork and spoon over the glaze.
notes: Food safety: cook pork to 70°C and keep raw pork away from ready-to-eat food.
Check the tamari label is gluten-free.
